hypotheses.justification: This follows from hF₂, hF₃ and h23. For f ∈ F, h23 gives J₁ f = J₂ (J₃ f) - J₃ (J₂ f). By hF₃ and then hF₂, J₂ (J₃ f) ∈ F. By hF₂ and then hF₃, J₃ (J₂ f) ∈ F. So J₁ f ∈ F by `F.sub_mem`. The proof then goes through unchanged after `have hF₁ := ...`. Only one of hF₁, hF₂, hF₃ can be deleted at a time: each is derived from the other two.

This follows from hF₁, hF₃ and h31. For f ∈ F, h31 gives J₂ f = J₃ (J₁ f) - J₁ (J₃ f). Both terms lie in F by hF₁ and hF₃, so J₂ f ∈ F by `F.sub_mem`. The rest of the proof is unchanged. This cannot be combined with deleting hF₁ or hF₃.

This follows from hF₁, hF₂ and h12. For f ∈ F, h12 gives J₃ f = J₁ (J₂ f) - J₂ (J₁ f). Both terms lie in F by hF₁ and hF₂, so J₃ f ∈ F by `F.sub_mem`. The rest of the proof is unchanged. This cannot be combined with deleting hF₁ or hF₂.

hypotheses.binder: (hskew₃ : ∀ x ∈ F, ∀ y ∈ F, B (J₃ x) y = -B x (J₃ y))
hypotheses.justification: This follows from hskew₁, hskew₂, h12, hlin, hsymm and the invariance hypotheses. The proof already derives hBsub (subtraction in the first argument, from hlin) and hBsub' (subtraction in the second argument, from hlin and hsymm). For x, y ∈ F, all of J₁J₂x, J₂J₁x, J₁J₂y and J₂J₁y lie in F. Then B (J₃ x) y = B (J₁J₂x - J₂J₁x) y = B (J₁J₂x) y - B (J₂J₁x) y = -B (J₂x) (J₁y) + B (J₁x) (J₂y) = B x (J₂J₁y) - B x (J₁J₂y) = -B x (J₁J₂y - J₂J₁y) = -B x (J₃ y). The steps use h12, hBsub, hskew₁ and hskew₂ twice each, hBsub', and h12 again. Proving this right after hBsub' leaves the rest of the proof unchanged. Only one of hskew₁, hskew₂, hskew₃ can be deleted at a time.

hypotheses.binder: (hskew₁ : ∀ x ∈ F, ∀ y ∈ F, B (J₁ x) y = -B x (J₁ y))
hypotheses.justification: This is the same argument with h23 (J₁ = J₂J₃ - J₃J₂ on F): B (J₁ x) y = B (J₂J₃x) y - B (J₃J₂x) y = B x (J₃J₂y) - B x (J₂J₃y) = -B x (J₁ y). It uses hskew₂, hskew₃, hBsub and hBsub', which come from hlin and hsymm. The rest of the proof is unchanged. This cannot be combined with deleting hskew₂ or hskew₃.

hypotheses.binder: (hskew₂ : ∀ x ∈ F, ∀ y ∈ F, B (J₂ x) y = -B x (J₂ y))
hypotheses.justification: This is the same argument with h31 (J₂ = J₃J₁ - J₁J₃ on F): B (J₂ x) y = B (J₃J₁x) y - B (J₁J₃x) y = B x (J₁J₃y) - B x (J₃J₁y) = -B x (J₂ y). It uses hskew₁, hskew₃, hBsub and hBsub'. The rest of the proof is unchanged. This cannot be combined with deleting hskew₁ or hskew₃.
